tariff_level.t: Few or no tariffs; free trade benefits most people.
yes: Removing most tariffs on imports

tariff_level.t: Low tariffs, used mainly against countries that break trade rules.
yes: Tariffs of about 5% or less on most goods
Targeted tariffs on rule-breakers, like countries dumping cheap steel

tariff_level.t: Moderate tariffs on many goods to protect key US industries.
yes: Tariffs of about 10–25% on goods like steel, cars and electronics

tariff_level.t: High tariffs on most imports to bring manufacturing back, even if prices rise.
yes: Tariffs of 25% or more on most imports
Accepting higher prices for US-made goods
no: Lowering tariffs to keep prices down

tariff_price_tradeoff.t: Lower prices matter more than protecting factory jobs with tariffs.
yes: Keeping tariffs low so cars and appliances stay cheaper
no: Tariffs that raise those prices by 10%

tariff_price_tradeoff.t: Tariffs to protect factory jobs are worth it only if prices rise about 2% to 3%.
yes: Small tariffs with a small price effect

tariff_price_tradeoff.t: Protecting factory jobs is worth prices about 10% higher on goods like cars and appliances.
yes: Tariffs that add about 10% to cars and appliances to keep factory jobs here

tariff_authority.t: Only Congress should set tariffs, by passing laws.
yes: Requiring a vote of Congress for any tariff
no: Presidents setting tariffs on their own

tariff_authority.t: Congress sets tariffs, but the president can add them in a true emergency.
yes: Emergency tariffs by a president, with Congress setting the rest
no: Presidents setting tariffs whenever they choose

tariff_authority.t: The president should set tariffs whenever the president judges it's in the national interest.
yes: Broad presidential power over tariffs, for any president

tariff_authority_cases: A president should need Congress to do this: {case}.
A president should be able to do this without a vote of Congress: {case}.

trade_agreements.t: The US should sign tariff-cutting deals with as many countries as possible.
yes: New free trade agreements with many countries

trade_agreements.t: Sign more trade deals, but only with strong labor and environmental rules.
yes: Trade deals with enforceable labor and environmental standards

trade_agreements.t: Sign trade deals only with close allies.
yes: Deals with countries like Canada, Japan and European nations

trade_agreements.t: No more trade deals; pull out of existing ones where possible.
yes: Withdrawing from trade agreements like the one with Canada and Mexico

trade_jobs_tradeoff.t: Make trade deals that help the country overall, even if some regions lose jobs.
yes: Trade deals with overall gains despite local job losses
no: Blocking deals to protect existing jobs

trade_jobs_tradeoff.t: Make those trade deals only with major help for workers who lose jobs.
yes: Large retraining, wage insurance and relocation aid for affected workers
no: Deals with no help for workers

trade_jobs_tradeoff.t: Protecting existing US jobs comes first.
yes: Turning down deals that would cost US industries jobs
no: Trade deals that shift jobs abroad, even with overall gains

china_trade.t: Trade freely with China, as with other countries.
yes: Normal trade in goods and technology with China

china_trade.t: Limit trade with China only in sensitive technology.
yes: Restrictions on advanced chips and military goods
no: Moving other production out of China

china_trade.t: Limit sensitive technology and move production of essentials out of China.
yes: Chip limits
Moving medicine and electronics production out of China

china_trade.t: Cut off most trade with China.
yes: Ending most imports from and exports to China

china_ownership.t: Chinese companies should be able to own US businesses, farmland and apps like any foreign company.
yes: Treating Chinese buyers like other foreign investors

china_ownership.t: Chinese companies can own US businesses, except in defense and personal data.
yes: Blocking Chinese ownership in defense and data-heavy businesses

china_ownership.t: No Chinese ownership of farmland, key technology or popular apps; other businesses are fine.
yes: Banning Chinese purchases of farmland
Forcing sale of apps like TikTok

china_ownership.t: Ban Chinese ownership of US businesses entirely.
yes: Barring any China-based company from owning US businesses
no: Any Chinese ownership in the US

industrial_policy.t: Government should pay companies to build factories in many industries.
yes: Subsidies and tax credits for chips, batteries and many other industries

industrial_policy.t: Pay companies to build factories only in industries vital to national security.
yes: Subsidies for chips and defense-related production

industrial_policy.t: The market should decide where investment goes.
yes: Ending industry-specific subsidies like the chip program

buy_american.t: Federal agencies should buy the best value, wherever it's made.
yes: Ending Buy American rules for most purchases

buy_american.t: Buy American only for military and security needs.
yes: US-made requirements for defense purchases

buy_american.t: Buy American if it costs no more than about 25% extra.
yes: Paying up to a 25% premium for US-made vehicles, steel and equipment

buy_american.t: Always buy American, even at much higher cost.
yes: US-made requirements regardless of price
no: Buying foreign goods to save money

offshoring_penalty.t: Companies that move US jobs abroad should face penalties.
yes: Higher taxes and losing government contracts for offshoring

offshoring_penalty.t: No penalty, but end tax breaks that make moving jobs abroad cheaper.
yes: Closing tax breaks for overseas operations

offshoring_penalty.t: Companies should decide where to operate.
yes: No penalties or special taxes for offshoring
no: Penalizing companies that move jobs abroad

export_controls.t: Companies should be free to sell advanced technology to anyone.
yes: Ending chip export limits on China and Russia

export_controls.t: Block sales of technology with clear military uses only.
yes: Blocking military-use technology

export_controls.t: Block sales of most advanced technology to rivals, even if US companies lose sales.
yes: Broad limits on selling top chips and tech to China and Russia
no: Letting companies sell advanced chips to rivals

friend_shoring.t: Allies should get clearly lower tariffs than other countries.
yes: Much lower tariffs for Canada, Japan and European countries

friend_shoring.t: Allies should get somewhat lower tariffs.
yes: Modest tariff preferences for allies

friend_shoring.t: Treat all trading partners the same.
yes: The same tariffs for allies and others

friend_shoring.t: Allies should face tariffs too if they sell more to us than they buy.
yes: Tariffs on allies with trade surpluses with the US
